answer: The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28.0 pages (based on 18 original papers; SD ≈ 7.4; median 27.5; range 16–45), whereas the average length of original papers in Psychology is 11.2 pages (based on 97 original papers; SD ≈ 6.3; median 9; range 1–31). In other words, original papers in Experimental Economics are on average markedly longer than original papers in Psychology.

payload.hypothesis: The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28.0 pages (n=18) and that in Psychology is 11.2 pages (n=97); thus Experimental Economics original papers are on average markedly longer (~2.5x) than Psychology original papers.
payload.workflow: 1) Inspected both CSVs; only meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927x57) contains required fields length/project/discipline (the replication_success CSV lacks them). 2) Grouping by project: Experimental Economics = project=='ee' (18 papers, coincides exactly with discipline=='Economics'); Psychology = project=='rpp' (97 papers, Social 55 + Cognitive 42). The discipline field has no 'Psychology' category, so project is the only operational grouping matching the question. 3) Unit of analysis = each original paper: deduplicated by id (927 rows -> 141 unique papers; duplication only in ml1/ml3, not in ee/rpp). 4) Verified length has 0 missing values (927/927), no imputation needed. 5) Computed per-group mean, SD, median, min, max of length at study level and confirmed row-level vs study-level means are identical for ee/rpp. 6) Final result: ee mean=28.0 pages (n=18, sd=7.37, median=27.5); rpp mean=11.2 pages (n=97, sd=6.30, median=9.0).
